summary: A first-person narrator recounts leaving conventional schooling: they manipulated school records to enter the intended grade, found the classes mediocre, and at fourteen began spending time in University of Minnesota libraries, which felt welcoming and free of the public library's noisy children. They planned to enroll in a college program for high schoolers at sixteen, and say they were busy running their own business and with 'the Group.' The excerpt ends with Monica and the narrator discussing a news photo of children being led out of a house, with a boy named Wilson in front, as his father's reaction is debated.
one_line: A narrator describes leaving regular school for University of Minnesota libraries and a planned college program, then a news photo of Wilson being led from a house.
key_facts: The narrator changed schools and claimed their records got messed up so they could enter the intended grade instead of repeating the one they never finished.
The narrator says that taking a GED test would have been simpler, but that option was not available to them.
The narrator describes school as a prison system combined with a mass babysitting operation.
The narrator started hanging out at the libraries at the University of Minnesota once they hit fourteen.
The University of Minnesota libraries had guest wifi and no little kids running around screaming, unlike the public library.
The narrator says articles found on Google Scholar that cost thirty-five bucks are free when accessed from a library computer.
In 2013, the original 'Garden of Earthly Delights' painting was seen up close by Diana after waiting in line for hours.
A college student told the narrator about a program where high school kids could take college classes and get free textbooks.
The narrator planned to try for that program next year, when they would be sixteen and eligible.
The narrator says they had their own business to run and were involved with 'the Group.'
Monica comments that Wilson's father must be going crazy while looking at a picture of kids being led out of a house.
Wilson is shown in front in the photo, looking like he just woke up and was wondering why people with guns were in his front yard.
